To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the parental evaluation of the PWSs was the best method of evaluation of the PDL treatment outcome in children, 2) the L*a*b* measurement was not useful in the evaluation of the PDS treatment, 3) the visual inspection by the blinded observers was not a reliable method for the evaluation of the response to the PDL treatment in children.
the assessment of port wine stains in children following multiple pulsed dye laser treatments is difficult, and the best way to assess the treatment is to ask parents to assess it.

the L*a*b* method was not useful in evaluating port wine stains previously treated with pulsed-dye lasers, parental assessment may lead one to overtreat, and that visual inspection of serial photography is a more useful way to assess port wine stains previously exposed to pulsed-dye treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method for the assessment of the efficacy of laser treatment of PWSs.
the development of an objective method to measure the efficacy of pulsed-dye lasers in the treatment of port wine stains in children.
the evaluation of PWSs following multiple PDL treatments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a visual evaluation by blinded observers is the only reliable method for assessing the response to pulsed dye laser therapy in PWSs.
a visual inspection by blinded observers may be the most accurate and reliable method to evaluate the clinical response to PDL treatment in PWSs previously treated.
there is no objective measure of response to PDL treatment for pediatric PWSs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the L*a*b* measurement of PWSs does not correlate with the visual perception of PWS lightening.
parental assessment is not a reliable method to evaluate the response to PDL treatment in the PWS.
parental assessment of the response to PDL treatment of PWS in children is not an adequate substitute for a clinical assessment by an experienced clinician.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the clinical evaluation of PWS response to PDL treatment is not as objective as previously assumed.
the visual inspection of photographs by blinded observers is a more reliable method for assessing PDL response than either parental assessment or objective assessment by L*a*b*.
there is a lack of correlation between the objective measurements (L*a*b* color measurements) and the clinical assessment (visual inspection) of PDL treatment response in children with PWSs.
